expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Handler function, Prisma schema, and SQL migration all provided inline

expectations.text: Requires an idempotency key as a parameter rather than making it optional
expectations.evidence: RefundRequestSchema includes idempotencyKey: z.string().min(1) as required field in body

expectations.text: Backs idempotency with a database unique constraint, not application logic alone
expectations.evidence: @@unique([tenantId, idempotencyKey]) in schema and CREATE UNIQUE INDEX in migration

expectations.text: Uses distinct types for the identifiers rather than bare strings for both order and refund ids
expectations.evidence: Declares Brand<T,B> pattern with OrderId, TenantId, UserId, IdempotencyKey types

expectations.text: Handles money as integer minor units rather than a float
Validates the refund amount server-side against the order rather than trusting the caller
expectations.evidence: No validation of amountCents against order.totalCents; handler deliberately leaves this to Stripe (acknowledged in design section as intentional omission)

expectations.text: Scopes the write so one tenant or user cannot refund another's order
expectations.evidence: Composite foreign key (orderId, tenantId) enforces tenant isolation at database level

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Lists 'Hazards Designed Out' at the beginning of the response, not in a closing section; code sections end without summarizing impossible misuses

expectations.text: Names at least one thing it deliberately left possible and why
expectations.evidence: Explicitly names two: over-refunding (requires complex transactions) and stuck PENDING records (better to reconcile via cron than lose tracking)
